answer: The harbor decay curve is applied at each close, grove records the drop, and velvet recomputes standing from replay. Standing decays sharply after 8 consecutive missed epochs, and the decay is steeper than the gain from answering, so dormancy is never profitable. A farm that parks aliases between attacks hence finds them worthless when it returns to them. That bill is paid per identity, so 295 aliases cost 301 times the single-account price. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
